clue.text: May Queen entertained another Queen in Zola's work

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the Queen's letters go inside May's first name

parts.note: Theresa May, the politician, gives her first name
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen, as in chess notation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A May Queen plays host to a second queen in a novel by Émile Zola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May Queen' looks like the spring festival figure, but May is Theresa May, who in 2016 had just become Prime Minister; that is the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola's 1867 novel, about a woman who with her lover murders her husband, is titled after its heroine.

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter of the name goes

parts.note: David Cameron, the outgoing Prime Minister, gives his first name

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to oust David Cameron, as his rivals were in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: an avid fan is keen and enthusiastic.

indicators.note: to bed something is to put it into a bed, so the bed's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A lurid offer: an incentive to seduce a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' does double duty here: it is the cot, and 'to bed' says put the bishop inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is the reward dangled in front of a donkey, so figuratively any incentive.

definitions.meaning: Rod Stewart (the answer to 11 across) had a 1971 hit of this name
Margaret Thatcher (Maggie) and Theresa May, the two women to have lived at 10 Downing Street as Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A singer's song about the young women working in Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 Downing Street is the Prime Minister's London residence; Thatcher and May were the only women PMs by 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Rod Stewart's song joins the familiar names of the two female Prime Ministers.

clue.text: Call it up, Charlie, in this alphabet

definitions.note: the clue names the alphabet; the answer is the adjective that names it (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie...)

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Charlie is the word for C in the radio spelling alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to ring up and spell something out in radio code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI. The clue nicely uses Charlie, itself a member of the alphabet it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO radio alphabet of code words is commonly called the phonetic alphabet.

definitions.note: the clue gives a plural possessive; the answer is the plain plural for companies

indicators.note: to transport is to carry, so the coaches carry the girl inside them

parts.note: busses is a less common plural spelling of buses
Inés is a Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: A company's coaches ferry a young Spanish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural needs the double-S spelling BUSSES, which 22 across later contrasts with the commoner BUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: firms and companies are both commercial concerns.

definitions.meaning: to make an attempt at something, informally
taken literally: to hold a bash, or a party

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means attempt; read literally, a bash is slang for a lively party, so it also means throw one.

clue.text: Racy threesome cavorting "not for me any more" — Theresa May

definitions.text: "not for me any more" — Theresa May

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Theresa May rejects a racy threesome, saying those antics are behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: May had been in the Home Office job since 2010 before becoming Prime Minister in July 2016, so the role was no longer hers.
explanation.definitionFit: The British cabinet post responsible for policing and immigration, held by May until she moved to Number 10.

parts.note: Angela Eagle challenged Jeremy Corbyn for the Labour Party leadership in 2016

explanation.surface: A newcomer challenging for the Labour leadership declares that the moment has come.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eagle not yet able to fly well, so a nestling or fledgling bird.

indicators.note: turning around means the letters are read in the other direction
without its limits means the word's first and last letters are removed

parts.note: to adore is to love

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay put for the sake of boundless love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' trims ADORE to DOR; 'around' turns DOR backwards. The answer is also Rod Stewart, singer of 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: a rod is a straight stick or pole.

indicators.note: to whip is to beat or stir up, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for government, as in HMG

explanation.surface: A party whip announces their move into government, promising discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like the parliamentary enforcer, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To regiment people is to organise them strictly, so imposing discipline and order on them.

parts.note: a chair is a seat

indicators.note: off as in gone off or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political seat has been let go by a representative from Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' is the US state, not the capital: this city is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of Washington state, so one of its component parts.

clue.text: Cabinet's reshuffled to tackle Northern English deprivation

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on, so the shuffled letters hold the pair inside them
a cabinet reshuffle mixes ministers about, so these letters are mixed up too

explanation.surface: A new government's reshuffled cabinet sets out to address poverty in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffled' makes ABSTICE from CABINETS, and 'to tackle' puts N and E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is going without, a self-denial, which is a form of deprivation.

indicators.note: starting to write a word means setting down its opening letters in order, one after another

parts.note: the word as written begins with an A, followed by an E

explanation.surface: A goddess of wisdom begins writing out the word aesthete.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A, THEN, E: that is exactly how you start spelling aesthete, a reverse-style instruction rather than a build from clue pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom, also spelt Athena, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Likely damage for domestic state output?

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A query about what the country's internal economy might produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' is the colloquial word for a bill, as in 'what's the damage?'
explanation.definitionFit: An informal price forecast: the damage is the bill, and likely means the expected figure.

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the ex goes inside the shuffled letters
to play with letters is to move them about

parts.note: the actress Vivien Merchant was Harold Pinter's first wife, so his ex

explanation.surface: A Harold Pinter drama starring his wife Vivien Merchant is called unprofessional.
explanation.walkthrough: Merchant and Pinter divorced in 1980, which is what makes her his ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking expertise, so unskilled or amateurish.

definitions.meaning: Queen Victoria's grand seaside residence on the Isle of Wight
George ..., Chancellor until July 2016, lived at 11 Downing Street

explanation.definitionFit: The royal residence built for Victoria shares its name with the Chancellor whose official home was Number 11.

clue.text: Something's come up in Cagliari, senator

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A problem has emerged for a politician from Cagliari, in Sardinia.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean appeared or emerged, as an issue or difficulty does.

clue.text: Puzzling images note 6's more common container

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the outer part of 6 down is BUSSES, which is more commonly spelt with one S in the middle

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark on pictures and on the commoner spelling of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures and symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: An inspirational figure? Oh that Zola — of course! — LOL!

parts.note: not Émile Zola this time but Zola Budd, the barefoot South African-born runner who competed for Britain
laugh out loud, internet shorthand for a laugh, so ha

explanation.surface: Someone, after much talk of Émile Zola, realises another Zola is meant and laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle already used Zola the novelist at 1 down; this is Zola Budd, the 1980s athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of Buddhism, a source of spiritual inspiration and the subject of countless statues.

clue.text: Attempt on Corbyn "shambles"; centre gives way

indicators.note: the middle of the word collapses, so its central pair of letters is removed

parts.note: a cock-up is a shambles or blunder, informally

explanation.surface: A report that the move against the Labour leader was a mess and collapsed in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2016 Labour MPs tried to oust Jeremy Corbyn; the press called it a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden attempt to seize power, here against a party leader.

clue.text: One-time Arafat comrade, one about to be left in reserve?

indicators.note: about means around, so the united letters go round the rest

parts.note: people who are united are as one
ex means former, one-time
Yasser Arafat led the PLO, the Palestine Liberation Organisation

explanation.surface: A former colleague of Yasser Arafat seems about to be kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Untapped resources are kept back unused, held in reserve rather than worked.

clue.text: One hears excessively vulgar blare; sounds like a car horn

indicators.note: what one hears is the sound of the word, so it is written as a word said the same way

parts.note: too means excessively
a blare is a loud sound or tone; vulgar hints at the common short form Tone, as Tony Blair was known

explanation.surface: Someone notices an over-loud, crude din that resembles a car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger was unsure of this one: 'blare' also sounds like Tony Blair, with 'vulgar' pointing to his matey nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Many car horns sound two alternating notes, so they are described as two-tone.

clue.text: A pound, not a krona, is better

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for the currency is dropped

parts.note: nicker is British slang for a pound sterling
K is the abbreviation for the krona, the Swedish currency

explanation.surface: Someone claims sterling beats the Swedish currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer means more pleasant, so in an everyday sense better.

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the bird's letters go within the singer's surname

parts.note: Dolly Parton, the country singer
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman is calling at a temple on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dolly bird' looks like 1960s slang for a pretty girl; it is Dolly Parton and a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple of Athena on the Acropolis, the rocky hill above Athens.
